label: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017
output:
@Mikaela yeah we’re on 10 in 7 this season. 290 cows, mostly 3-way crossbreds. Started 21 Sept just after mating got going. We skip the Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday arvo milkings plus Sunday arvo, so four afternoons off a week. Mornings still 5.15 every day.

Production’s down about 6% on milksolids for the same weeks last year, going off the Fonterra app. Our rep had said expect 8–10, so it’s better than that, but it’s still a real 6% and I’m not going to pretend otherwise. Funny, our vet was keener on it than the rep too. I’d say the truth is somewhere in the middle — it’s a good tool if you run it properly, not a silver bullet.

Cells did jump. From 110k to about 180k for the first 3 weeks, back round 135k now. Not mental, but enough that you know about it. You have to be on your game with teat spraying and checking cows on the skip days or it bites you. We had a heifer get mastitis on a skipped arvo and I didn’t spot it till next morning. Lost a quarter. That’s the bit I’d want you to hear properly, because you can get away with a fair bit on 10 in 7 but not slack checking.

Good bits are real too. Lame cows way down — 4 on the lame list now vs 11 this time last year. Our long walk to the back paddocks is 1.8km, so the arvos off are doing a job. Cows came round quicker than I thought, about 4 days of bellowing at the gate then fine. Kieran, our 2IC, said it’s the first spring he hasn’t wanted to quit by October. And the first skipped Sunday arvo Dave and me went to Hamilton to see the grandkids — first Sunday off in spring in 20 odd years. That was pretty bloody good.

Honestly, I wouldn’t go back. The hours alone are worth the 6% to me. If Tom’s knees are bad the arvos off will help more than anything. But it’s not set and forget — you’ve got to have the checks and the teat spraying nailed, and someone has to actually look at the cows on the skip days. I’m not trying to talk you into it and have you cursing me in March, so go in eyes open.

Come have a look at our shed rosters and numbers at the field day on the 19th. I’ll bring them. Ring me if you want to yarn about it, easier than texting.
